sideFindings: A LIVE DEFECT IN THE PRISTINE BUILD, found while building the missions and NOT attributable to any mutant — mission /tmp/tom-G. `readManifest` (src/lib/conformance.ts) is fence-aware: it toggles on ``` / ~~~ and refuses to count a `Rule conformance` heading written inside a code fence. `textOutsideManifest` is fence-BLIND: its `findIndex` takes the first line that matches anywhere in the file. Put a fenced illustration of the manifest format above the real table — the obvious thing to do when documenting your own deliverable — and the two disagree: the section removed runs from the FENCED heading to the real one, so the real table survives in the text the symbol is looked up in, and `file:<self>#<the row's own slug>` is accepted. Measured: `check --json --strict --path /tmp/tom-G` exits 0, verdict `clean`, 0 conformance gaps, on a mission whose floor.md line 38 reads `| state-event-sourcing | applied | file:runward/floor.md#state-event-sourcing |`. That is RWD-2026-0002's universal green key, reachable today with no mutation at all. Scope, checked: no shipped template does this — templates/mission/*.md and runward/*.md each carry exactly one, non-fenced heading — so it is operator-reachable, not on by default.

Once `circularEvidence` lets a self-pointer through, nothing downstream stops it: `symbolPresent(content, symbol)` runs against the FULL file, table included, so the pointer's own text in its own row satisfies it (measured on /tmp/tom-I, where `alphabeta` exists only inside the pointer). `textOutsideManifest` is the single barrier, which is why five of its eleven survivors move the verdict.

verdicts.argument: `raw` is assigned unconditionally as the first statement of the `try`. The only path that skips that assignment is a throw inside `readFileSync`, and the `catch` returns a literal without ever reading `raw`. No read of `raw` can therefore observe its initialiser: the initialiser is dead on every path, for every file and every mission, independently of any reachability argument about the caller.

verdicts.evidence: Identical `check --json --strict` payload on all nine missions, including /tmp/tom-H, which was built for this mutant: the deliverable runward/floor.md is `chmod 000`. Observed there (pristine AND mutated, identically): the gate never emits JSON at all — 0 bytes on stdout, process exit 1, and on stderr `✗ EACCES: permission denied, open '/tmp/tom-H/runward/floor.md'`. The unreadable-file case is stopped upstream and never reaches this catch. Hand-applied on tom-B: `mutants 2: status 1 · exit 1 conformance 1 · 4713 bytes`, identical to pristine.
verdicts.argument: Two independent reasons, either sufficient. (1) The `catch` cannot be entered on any call this code can receive. `textOutsideManifest` is called only from `circularEvidence`, only when `abs === self`, i.e. on the deliverable whose rows `evidenceReport` is iterating — and `evidenceReport` obtained those rows from an UNGUARDED `readFileSync(join(missionDir, deliverable), "utf8")` a few statements earlier, in the same process, on the same inode. A file that cannot be read there yields no rows, no pointer and no call; a file that can be read there is still readable microseconds later. So `readFileSync(abs)` inside this function cannot throw. This is a CALLER-COUPLED equivalence: it holds because of where the function is called from, not because of what the function does. It would become live the day `textOutsideManifest` is called on a path the caller has not already read. (2) Even if the catch WERE entered, emptying it changes nothing: `raw` keeps its `""` initialiser, `"".split("\n")` is `[""]`, `findIndex` returns -1, and the pristine `start === -1` branch returns `[""].join("\n")` — the empty string, which is exactly what the pristine `catch { return ""; }` returns. The mutant reaches the same value by a longer route.

Identical `check --json --strict` payload on all nine missions (ledgers reports/mutation/probe-mission-{A..I}.jsonl), including tom-B and tom-I, whose manifests are written specifically so that the `start === -1` branch can be reached. Hand-applied in combination with the one mutation that DOES reach that branch (scratchpad/apply.mjs, tom-B and tom-I): `mutants 5: status 0 · exit 0 conformance 0 · 4375 bytes` and `mutants 5+6: status 0 · exit 0 conformance 0 · 4375 bytes` — byte-identical, so the early return carries no decision even once the branch is taken.
verdicts.argument: Two independent reasons. (1) `start === -1` cannot happen on any call this code can receive. `textOutsideManifest` has one caller, `circularEvidence`, which calls it only on the branch `abs === self` — that is, on the deliverable whose rows `evidenceReport` has just parsed. Those rows come from `parseManifest` / `readManifest` (src/lib/conformance.ts), which returns zero rows unless it found EXACTLY ONE non-fenced line matching `/^#{1,6}\s+Rule conformance/i`. `textOutsideManifest` runs the byte-identical regex over the byte-identical file (same inode: `self` is the realpath of `join(missionDir, deliverable)`), through `findIndex`, with no fence filter — so it searches a superset of the lines `readManifest` searched and necessarily finds at least that same line. No rows means no pointer, which means no call. Hence `start >= 0` on every reachable call. (2) Even in the counterfactual where `start === -1` is taken, dropping the early return cannot change the decision. With `start = -1` the loop starts at `i = 0`, and the manifest's own `Rule conformance` heading matches `/^#{1,6}\s/`, so `end` is always at most that heading's index and strictly less than `lines.length`. The value returned, `[...lines.slice(0, -1), ...lines.slice(end)]`, is therefore a SUPERSET of every line of the file (the last line is restored by `slice(end)`, the rest by `slice(0, -1)`). The sole consumer is `outside.includes(symbol)`, and it was already true on the full text the pristine branch returns — the file contains the manifest row that carries this very pointer, and that row contains the symbol's literal text. True before, true after. Observed on tom-B and tom-I.

verdicts.evidence: Identical payload on all nine missions (ledgers reports/mutation/probe-mission-{A..I}.jsonl), tom-B and tom-I included. For contrast, the SAME `join("\n") → join("")` mutation on the reachable return (line 376) flips tom-E and tom-I from exit 1 to exit 0, so the harness is demonstrably sensitive to this class of change.
verdicts.argument: Two independent reasons. (1) `start === -1` cannot happen on any call this code can receive. `textOutsideManifest` has one caller, `circularEvidence`, which calls it only on the branch `abs === self` — that is, on the deliverable whose rows `evidenceReport` has just parsed. Those rows come from `parseManifest` / `readManifest` (src/lib/conformance.ts), which returns zero rows unless it found EXACTLY ONE non-fenced line matching `/^#{1,6}\s+Rule conformance/i`. `textOutsideManifest` runs the byte-identical regex over the byte-identical file (same inode: `self` is the realpath of `join(missionDir, deliverable)`), through `findIndex`, with no fence filter — so it searches a superset of the lines `readManifest` searched and necessarily finds at least that same line. No rows means no pointer, which means no call. Hence `start >= 0` on every reachable call. (2) Even if the branch were taken, the separator cannot change the decision. The branch returns the whole file, which necessarily contains the manifest row carrying this very pointer, and that row contains the symbol's literal text on a single line. Joining with `""` instead of `"\n"` only ever ADDS substrings to a concatenation — every within-line substring survives — so `outside.includes(symbol)` is true under both separators. (The one corner where the row's spelling and the parsed symbol differ is a symbol written with backticks, which `readManifest` strips before the grammar runs; that corner still needs the unreachable branch, so it changes nothing here.)

verdicts.evidence: Identical `check --json --strict` payload on all nine missions — self-gate, tom-A … tom-I — including tom-D and tom-G, whose deliverables end on a content line, and tom-F, the control board carrying five different pointer shapes at once (4965 bytes of payload, two violations, unchanged). Ledgers: reports/mutation/probe-mission-{A..I}.jsonl. Hand-applied on tom-B: `mutants 8: status 1 · exit 1 conformance 1 · 4713 bytes`, identical to pristine.
verdicts.argument: Two independent reasons. (1) The extra iteration evaluates `lines[lines.length]`, which is `undefined`; `RegExp.prototype.test` coerces it to the string "undefined", which cannot match `/^#{1,6}\s/` — and the loop body runs only on a match, so nothing executes. (2) Even if that phantom line DID match, the body would assign `end = lines.length`, which is exactly the value `end` already holds at that point (it is the initialiser, and the loop only reaches the extra iteration by never having broken). `lines.slice(lines.length)` is `[]` either way, so the returned string is identical. No file and no mission can separate the two versions.

verdicts.evidence: Mission /tmp/tom-C. Pristine: exit 1, verdict `gaps`, conformance 1, `[Floor] state-event-sourcing: typed pointer file:runward/floor.md#state-event-sourcing — this is the manifest that carries the row, and "state-event-sourcing" appears only in its Rule conformance table …`. Mutant applied: exit 0, verdict `clean`, conformance 0. Probe: `OBSERVABLE: exit-code` in reports/mutation/probe-mission-C.jsonl. The only thing tom-C adds is one editorial note between the heading and the table — `> Status vocabulary: applied / deviated / n/a — rationale in ADR # 2.` — whose `# 2` matches an unanchored `#{1,6}\s`. The end of the section is then read as that note, the whole table stays in the text searched, and the row proves itself. A blockquote a human would write while documenting their own manifest is enough.

Mission /tmp/tom-D, and this one runs the OTHER way — an honest mission turned red. tom-D states its fact BELOW the table, under a level-1 heading (`# 2. Proof against the success criterion`, followed by `The interaction log is append-only, keyed by request ID, and never mutated in place.`), and cites it as `file:runward/floor.md#"The interaction log is append-only, keyed by request ID"` — the one form of documentary self-evidence the gate advertises. Pristine: exit 0, verdict `clean`, conformance 0. Mutant applied: exit 1, verdict `gaps`, conformance 1, `[Floor] state-event-sourcing: typed pointer file:runward/floor.md#"The interaction log is append-only, keyed by request ID" — … appears only in its Rule conformance table …`. Probe: `OBSERVABLE: exit-code` in reports/mutation/probe-mission-D.jsonl. Mechanism, observed: `/^#{1,6}\S/` still matches `## …` (the quantifier backtracks to one `#` and `\S` eats the second), but never `# …`, so a level-1 section after the table stops ending the table and everything below it is thrown away.

Two missions, both flipping the exit code. /tmp/tom-E: the prose wraps a hyphenated compound across two lines (`The persistence adapter follows the reference stack's state-event` / `-sourcing conventions end to end.`) and the row cites `file:runward/floor.md#state-event-sourcing`. Pristine: exit 1, conformance 1, `… appears only in its Rule conformance table …`; mutant applied: exit 0, verdict `clean`, conformance 0 — joining the lines with nothing manufactures the symbol that the document does not contain. /tmp/tom-I reproduces it with a symbol absent from the file entirely (`alphabeta`, formed by gluing a line ending in `alpha` to a line starting `beta`): same flip, exit 1 → exit 0. Probes: `OBSERVABLE: exit-code` in reports/mutation/probe-mission-E.jsonl and reports/mutation/probe-mission-I.jsonl. Worth recording from tom-I: once `circularEvidence` lets a self-pointer through, the downstream `symbolPresent` check is satisfied by the pointer's OWN text in the row, so this function is the only thing standing between a manifest and self-proof.
